papers.title: Bioprinting and Preliminary Testing of Highly Reproducible Novel Bioink for Potential Skin Regeneration.
papers.abstract: Three-dimensional (3D) bioprinting is considered as a novel approach in biofabricating cell-laden constructs that could potentially be used to promote skin regeneration following injury. In this study, a novel crosslinked chitosan (CH)-genipin (GE) bioink laden with keratinocyte and human dermal fibroblast cells was developed and printed successfully using an extruder-based bioprinter. By altering the composition and degree of CH-GE crosslinking, bioink printability was further assessed and compared with a commercial bioink. Rheological analysis showed that the viscosity of the optimised bioink was in a suitable range that facilitated reproducible and reliable printing by applying low pressures ranging from 20-40 kPa. The application of low printing pressures proved vital for viability of cells loaded within the bioinks. Further characterisation using MTT assay showed that cells were still viable within the printed construct at 93% despite the crosslinking, processing and after subjecting to physiological conditions for seven days. The morphological study of the printed cells showed that they were mobile within the bioink. Furthermore, the multi-layered 3D printed constructs demonstrated excellent self-supportive structures in a consistent manner.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文不涉及任何人工智能技术，与AI生物打印方向无直接关联。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not embed AI/ML into any bioprinting workflow stage and focuses solely on bioink development and cell viability testing.

summary_zh.motivation: 开发可重复打印且支持细胞存活的生物墨水用于皮肤再生。
summary_zh.method: 制备壳聚糖-京尼平交联生物墨水，通过挤出式打印评估其印刷性和细胞活性。
summary_zh.result: 优化后的生物墨水在低压力下可重复打印，细胞存活率达93%。
summary_zh.validation: 通过流变学、MTT实验和形态学观察验证墨水性能。

summary_en.motivation: To develop a novel bioink with high reproducibility and cell viability for potential skin regeneration.
summary_en.method: A chitosan-genipin crosslinked bioink laden with keratinocytes and fibroblasts was prepared and extruder-based bioprinting was performed.
summary_en.result: The optimized bioink exhibited reliable printability at low pressures (20-40 kPa) and maintained cell viability at 93% after 7 days.
summary_en.validation: Rheological analysis, MTT assay, and morphological imaging were used to validate bioink printability and cell viability.
